name: Slit snow goggles
summary: Arctic peoples wore close-fitting eye shields of ivory, bone, antler or wood with narrow slits that cut snow glare while still letting them see.
description: A face-fitted opaque eye screen with narrow viewing slits admits a restricted field of vision while screening the eye from bright light. Different forms use wood, bone or antler; protection and visual field vary with aperture, fit and conditions.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.
why: Bright sunlight reflected off snow and ice causes painful snow blindness, so people needed to shield their eyes outdoors.
